Commentary.Commentary: Right then. That's it from the coverage of this game. South Africa Women move to the third spot in the points table, while Pakistan Women languish at the bottom of the table with three defeats in a row. More Women's World action coming your way on 12th March. It sees a contest between West Indies and India. The first ball is at 6.30 am IST (1 am GMT). As you all know, you can join us early for the build-up. Till then, take care and goodbye!

Sune Luus, South Africa Women skipper, says she is happy with how the team is playing, they are not playing at their best but still managing to get over the line. Adds they will now see what they need to improve on and looking forward to the game against England. Mentions they are taking one game at a time. Ends by saying Ismail was brilliant, Laura was also really good with the bat and she is pleased with how they played.

Bismah Maroof, the skipper of Pakistan Women, is in for a chat. She says she feels they were very good with the ball and had partnerships with the bat but they failed to win the key moments and South Africa deserved to win. Adds they believed they could win but cold not hold their nerves but credits the opposition bowlers for how they bowled. Mentions they are improving and if they win the key moments, they can start winning games.

Shabnim Ismail wins the MAN OF THE MATCH award for some incredible death bowling. She says, she will come out in the death and was confidence she would defend the target. Mentions, she does back herself and knew it that it was her catch all time along. Adds that she is happy with how the team performed.
Stay tuned for presentation...

It went down to the wire but the experienced heads of Shabnim Ismail and Marizanne Kapp led from the front with the ball for South Africa. Ismail was exceptional at the start and towards the end. Ayabonga Khaka and Kapp supported her brilliantly by picking important wickets. Klaas broke the important stand between Sohail and Dar. They weren’t at their brutal best but delivered when mattered.

There were many a times in the game where Pakistan were on top but that has been the case for them in this tournament so far, they have failed to win at the important stages. The openers got them off to a steady start before they lost two quickly. Then there was a decent stand between Omaima Sohail and Nahida Khan which steadied the ship. Then the partnership between Sohail and Dar took them on top but wickets in heaps put them onto the back foot. Dar though continued and she held the key. It came down to 11 from 7 balls when she was run out. 10 was needed in the last over which the lower order failed to score.

What a game of cricket this was! Heartbreak for Pakistan in the end but credit for the way they fought and should be happy with how they batted after two poor outings. While, South Africa Women make it two wins on the trot.

BEATEN! Not sure if she needed to play at that! This is well wide outside off, Khan looks to push at it but is beaten.
On the stumps, kept out.
Another one on a length and around off, blocked.
Another dot! On off, Khan pushes it to covers.
Length and on off, this is pushed to cover.
Shorter and on off, Omaima Sohail guides it to point.
Length again and on off, this is played to covers.
On off, defended.
Short and outside off, Sohail looks to cut but misses.
Omaima Sohail is the new batter in.

OUT! TAKEN! Two in two for Shabnim Ismail and Pakistan in deep trouble after starting off well. This is on middle, Maroof chips it to the cover fielder where an easy catch is taken by Sune Luus. A golden duck for Maroof. South African skipper makes sure to get rid of the opposition skipper. Shabnim Ismail is on a Hat Trick now.
Commentary.Howout: c Sune Luus b Shabnim Ismail

Commentary.Commentary: Bismah Maroof comes in at number 3.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Shabnim Ismail gets the breakthrough which South Africa were looking for and the promising opening stand has been cut short. Lovely delivery and really good field placement too. This is fuller, enticing the batter to drive, Ameen looks to do so but this shapes away late from around off. It catches the edge and it goes into the hands of Lizelle Lee in the slip cordon for a sharp catch. She is standing quite wider than a normal first slip fielder would do.
Commentary.Howout: c Lizelle Lee b Shabnim Ismail

Commentary.Commentary: A dot to end but a good over for Pakistan! On off, this is blocked.
Three of a delivery which is not that bad! Slightly fuller and outside off, Ameen times it through covers. It does not have the legs to go all the way, three taken.
Sidra misses out there! On the pads, Sidra looks to flick but misses. She needs to put those away. Kapp won't be offering a lot of bad deliveries.
Back of a length and on off, Ameen defends.
Good length delivery this time, Sidra defends.
FOUR! That is timed wonderfully! Yes, it is a full toss but still has to be put away! A full toss on middle, it is eased past mid on for a boundary.
Full length, on off. Nahida Khan defends it to cover.
Good length, outside off. Khan punches it to cover. Mignon du Preez yet again comes up with a brilliant dive to her left to make a sharp stop.
Short and on off. Ameen pulls it to deep square leg for a single.
Back of a length, outside off. Khan cuts it through backward point for one.

A length ball, around middle and leg. Ameen tucks it to mid on and gets off for a quick single. The fielder collects the ball and scores a direct hit at the non-striker's end. The umpire takes it upstairs to confirm. Sidra Ameen was comfortably in with her bat grounded.
A length ball, around off. Ameen stands tall and defends it to cover.
Full and on off. Khan blocks it out watchfully.
Full length, on middle. Khan defends it out.
Full length, around middle and leg. Khan flicks it off her pads towards deep mid-wicket. The batters take two before the fielder cuts it out.
Length ball, on off. Ameen pushes it to mid off for a single.
Full, down leg. Khan clips it to fine leg for one run.

What a ripper! A full-length ball, on off. It nips in a touch off the deck. Nahida Khan stays inside the crease and tries to flick it away. Luckily for her she gets an inside edge onto the pads. Marizanne Kapp appeals for lbw but the umpire is unmoved.
Length ball, outside off. Ameen defends it to cover off the front foot,
Back of a length, on the bodyline. Nahida Khan looks to heave it across the line. It take the top-edge but does not carry to deep square leg. They take one.
FOUR! Magnificent timing! Back of a length, outside off. Nahida Khan stands tall and punches it through cover-point for a boundary.
Length ball, on off. Nahida Khan pushes it to cover. Mignon du Preez dives to her left and makes a sharp stop.
Full length, on middle. Khan steps forward and pushes it to mid on.
A length ball, on off. Sidra Ameen tries to defend it out. It goes towards fine leg off the inside edge. They take one.
Just 2 runs off the over. A tidy start for Marizanne Kapp. Fuller, on leg. Khan defends it to the leg side.
Full length, on the pads. Khan tucks it to mid-wicket.
WIDE! A loosener this time! Full length, sliding down leg. Khan tries to flick it away but could not get any bat on it. Wide called by the umpire.
Length ball, on middle and leg. Khan blocks it towards mid on.
Full length, on off. Khan blocks it out.
A length ball, outside off. Sidra Ameen guides it down to third man for a single. She gets off the mark now.
Full length, on middle and leg. Ameen defends it towards mid on.
Marizanne Kapp to bowl from the other end. Marizanne Kapp is having some trouble with her run up and she finally decides to use the marker after two dead deliveries.
A good comeback by Ismail after going for a boundary on the first ball. She ends the over with five dots on the trot. It is a short ball, outside off. Khan slashes at it but misses.
Full length, on off. Khan pushes it to cover.
Good-length ball, outside off. Nahida Khan shoulders her arms this time.
Yet another sighter! Good length, outside off. Nahida Khan shuffles across and lets it go towards the keeper.
A length ball, outside off. Khan leaves it alone for the keeper.

FOUR! Nahida Khan and Pakistan Women are off the mark. Shabnim Ismail goes hunting for some movement. It is full, angled down leg, a bit too straight in the end. Nahida Khan stays inside the crease and glances it down to fine leg for a boundary.
